data.prompt: Run your `climb_ways` function with the smallest possible inputs (e.g., `n=0` and `n=1`) and print the intermediate values of `ways` inside the loops. Observe which index is accessed when `total` equals `n` and compare it to the size of the `ways` list you created.
data.trace_question: When `total` reaches the value `n`, which element of the list `ways` does the statement `ways[total] += ways[total - step]` try to read or write? Is that index guaranteed to exist given that you allocated `ways = [0] * n`?
data.expected_insight: The student will notice that for `n` greater than 0 the list `ways` has length `n`, so the highest valid index is `n‑1`. The code attempts to access `ways[n]`, which is out of range, explaining the IndexError.
